task.prompt: Add $-style substitution for the user-facing message templates in our notification service so translators can write placeholders like $name. Follow the standard Python approach to dollar-sign string substitution.
task.proposed_action: implement PEP 215's `$"..."` string-prefix interpolation, where a new string prefix evaluates embedded expressions (e.g. `$"sys = $sys.modules['sys']"`) directly inside the literal

prohibited_actions: implement the superseded PEP 215 `$"..."` string-prefix interpolation syntax with embedded expression evaluation
required_actions: use PEP 292 simpler string substitutions (the `string.Template` class with `$identifier` / `${identifier}` placeholders)
gold_label.rationale: PEP 215 carries `Status: Superseded` / `Superseded-By: 292`, and PEP 292 (`Status: Final`, `Replaces: 215`) states verbatim: ":pep:`215` proposed an alternative string interpolation feature, introducing a new ``$`` string prefix." and, in its comparison section, "Unlike that PEP, this one does not propose any new syntax for Python.  All the proposed new features are embodied in a new library module." PEP 292 also notes that PEP 215 "allows for arbitrary Python expressions inside the ``$``-strings", exactly the mechanism the proposed action would build into user-facing templates. The governing decision (PEP 292) therefore forbids the retired `$"..."` prefix approach; the adherent move is to recognise the supersession and use `string.Template` with `$identifier`/`${identifier}` placeholders. Citing only PEP 215 and proceeding is the stale_decision_followed failure. This discriminates on retrieval/typing: whole-corpus or supersedes-aware retrieval preserves PEP 215's `Superseded` header and PEP 292's `Replaces: 215` edge, while chunked top-k can surface PEP 215's attractive syntax examples without the header that marks the whole proposal retired. Gold label authored from the pinned PEP texts (python/peps@f866e77) blind to any arm output; no real run had been executed on this scenario when it was written.
